name: Inverter reboots mid-curtailment and forgets the limit
hypothesis: The hub has curtailed the inverter to hold a zero-export cap, then the inverter reboots and comes back at 100% WMaxLimPct — it forgot the limit and snaps to full output, blowing the cap. A hub that writes the limit once (on adoption) and never re-asserts it leaves the breach standing.
expected: Re-assert the limit after the inverter forgets it: detect the output jump via measurement and re-curtail within a cycle. Periodic idempotent control, not write-once.
fix: Re-send the active DER limit every control cycle (idempotent), not only on change; verify measured output against the commanded limit (orchestrator inverter adapter).
notes: TASK-077: migrated from the Go literal in cmd/dashboard/mayhem.go scenarios() (ID solar-reboot-forget). No teardown action: resetForScenario (run-loop machinery) uncurtails the inverter, matching the Go twin's empty teardown closure. ENCODING CAVEAT (recorded 2026-08-05, deliberately NOT changed): the tick-25 body {"WMaxLimPct_pct": 100} does not command a 100% ceiling. The sims encode that key as RawFromScaleSigned(N*100, SF) against SF=-2, i.e. N*10000, so any N above ~3.27 SATURATES at 32767 and 100 lands as a 327.67% ceiling. The scenario still measures what its hypothesis claims — the ceiling is released far above nameplate, the inverter snaps to full output, and the hub must re-assert — so the value is left alone: it is one of the two call sites sim/southbound/battery_pack.go's injectPackDispatch names as load-bearing on the defect, and correcting the encoding is a separate change with its own evidence. cmd/dashboard/scenariospec_migration_test.go pins the literal 100 at tick 25.
